tasks.short: Prepare objectives, outlines and lesson plans

steps.what: Set instructional program objectives and gather source materials
Prepare outlines and lesson plans from the objectives

loop.purpose: Draft a lesson sequence from selected materials
loop.input: Teacher objectives, session duration, constraints and source pack
loop.output: Source-linked outline and lesson plan draft
loop.check: Teacher checks sequence, timings, instruction accuracy and whether activities serve the stated objectives
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; finish manually if unsuitable
loop.why_not_simpler: A reusable approved plan is preferred, but a new sequence requires pedagogical wording and synthesis

steps.what: Check objectives, materials and lesson timings before adopting the plan

tasks.design: Use existing plan templates in the {DOCS} first. A bounded drafting aid turns the teacher's selected sources and brief into an outline; the teacher checks the draft and adopts an exact version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Producing a coherent first draft takes time after objectives have been chosen.
tasks.enabler_now: Document-to-course drafting tools can supply a first draft.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing suitable activities and realistic timings for the actual group.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher connects lesson choices to learner needs and available resources.
tasks.altitude: Less first-draft composition, with unchanged ownership of objectives and final plans.

evidence.claim: Easygenerator EasyAI creates a first course draft from documents or slide decks. This supports drafting, not autonomous lesson approval.
The allocation and saving for teacher-checked lesson-plan drafting are unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is planning, not lesson delivery, separate material adaptation or attendance administration.
Teacher produces the brief in s1: objectives, session length, learner level, available equipment, constraints and selected source versions. Capture and source selection retain all 30 hours.
s2 retains 30 hours for source checking, revision and fallback; missing information is returned to the teacher rather than guessed.
Test native templates and document-to-draft features before custom code. Reuse a suitable plan instead of generating another.
research_questions: Does total planning time fall after source selection and full teacher checking are included?

incremental.description: Maintain approved plan templates and source versions

approvals.approved_version: Exact lesson-plan file version, source list and activity timings reviewed in s3; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=30+30+20=80, gross 20 less 1 upkeep gives net 19. Low assumes mostly reusable plans or manual fallback; high requires the stated 50-hour drafting slice and review within retained time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Confer with teachers and professionals to plan lessons promoting development
Schedule agreed lessons with colleagues and confirm practical arrangements

tasks.design: Keep lesson planning conversations unchanged. Configure shared availability and invitation templates in the {CALENDAR}; the teacher enters the agreed requirements and checks the exact invitation before sending it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mail exchanges repeat availability checks after the substantive discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing shared-calendar scheduling can reduce those exchanges.
tasks.still_hard: Resolving competing teaching priorities and specialist access.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher negotiates educational trade-offs with colleagues.
tasks.altitude: A little less scheduling correspondence; collaborative planning remains the same.

reach.task: Spot room or specialist conflicts in proposed lesson slots
reach.learn: Calendar permissions and resource booking rules

evidence.claim: Shared calendars can support availability checks and reusable invitations; the estimated saving is a scenario.

assumptions: Boundary covers focal teacher conference and scheduling time; colleagues' meeting and calendar upkeep time is unchanged and earns no focal saving.

Teacher produces agreed aims and requirements during s1. In s2 the teacher captures participants, duration, resource needs and candidate dates; capture, review and exception time fit the retained 12 hours.

Colleagues maintain their ordinary availability calendars as today; no new availability-entry work is assumed. If calendars are incomplete, the teacher uses mail within retained exception time or gets no saving.
Test native calendar scheduling before custom code. No automated interpretation of colleagues' consent is used.
unknowns: Share of colleagues with current availability
research_questions: Does shared availability reduce mail time without moving capture work to colleagues?

already_counted.description: Enter requirements, resolve conflicts and check invitations

incremental.description: Maintain recurring slot and resource settings

approvals.approved_version: Exact participants, lesson dates, duration, location and invitation text checked before sending; any change requires a fresh check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=80+12=92. Gross 8 minus 1 upkeep is net 7. Low covers non-shared calendars and manual coordination; high assumes scheduling correspondence is 20 hours and falls to 12. Conference time stays 80.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Enforce policies and rules governing students through proportionate personal intervention

tasks.design: Keep interpretation and enforcement with the teacher. Consult existing rules in the {DOCS} as needed without introducing automatic sanctions or a new incident-recording baseline.
tasks.previous_blocker: The appropriate response depends on context and the student's explanation.
tasks.enabler_now: No technical change is needed to perform this boundary.
tasks.still_hard: Maintaining safety and fairness while de-escalating a disagreement.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher listens, explains and exercises proportionate judgement.

reach.task: Discuss consistent responses to recurring rule misunderstandings

evidence.claim: Rule enforcement in a class requires contextual judgement; no automatic sanction or saving is proposed.

assumptions: Boundary is live rule enforcement; separate institutional investigation or report writing is outside it.
Teacher observes behaviour and hears the student directly; existing policies come from the course provider. No structured incident flag is assumed.
Native document access remains as today; there is no build, new capture or upkeep, so incremental work is zero.
unknowns: Applicable provider rules and escalation arrangements
research_questions: Which recurring misunderstandings suggest that rules need clearer explanation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and incremental=0. Routine and difficult interventions both remain personal work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review course strengths and recommend revisions

steps.what: Gather instructional content, methods and student evaluations for review
Summarise evaluation themes and compare instructional strengths and weaknesses

loop.purpose: Group course feedback into provisional themes
loop.input: De-identified review pack with stable source identifiers
loop.output: Themes with supporting and contradictory excerpts
loop.check: Teacher checks each theme against original comments, retains minority concerns and distinguishes evidence from interpretation
loop.stop: One draft and one correction, then teacher summarises manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Native counts cover ratings; free-text concerns and instructional meaning need semantic reading

steps.what: Assess course strengths and weaknesses and recommend revision, development or elimination

tasks.design: Use native evaluation counts first and keep a versioned review pack in the {DOCS}. A bounded loop suggests source-linked comment themes; the teacher checks them, assesses the course and writes recommendations without delegating closure decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reading and grouping free-text evaluations is repetitive but context-sensitive.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded text summarisation can produce a checkable first theme list.
tasks.still_hard: Separating popularity from learning value and recognising minority access concerns.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher interprets evidence in the light of aims, teaching experience and learner needs.
tasks.altitude: Less first-pass grouping; course recommendations remain the teacher's judgement.

reach.task: Compare revision proposals across related courses
reach.learn: Qualitative evidence checking and curriculum trade-offs

evidence.claim: Source-linked comment grouping can assist a human review, but the proposed saving is unmeasured and not a result from the digest's tutoring trials.

assumptions: Boundary is focal teacher course review, not collecting new surveys, implementing revisions or deciding to close a course.

Students produce evaluations in the existing feedback process; no new response effort is required. Teacher s1 collects permitted comments, removes identifiers, assigns source IDs and records course/version/date; all capture time remains in its 25 hours.
If feedback cannot be safely prepared or traced, use manual review. s2 retains 15 hours for source checking and corrections.
Check native evaluation reporting before adding a loop. Do not use comments to score learners or staff.
unknowns: Feedback format and permission to use comments
research_questions: Does checked grouping retain important minority concerns while reducing total review time?

already_counted.description: Verify themes and correct omitted or distorted evidence

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=25+15+50=90. Gross 10 less 1 upkeep gives net 9. Low assumes little usable text or manual fallback; high assumes a 25-hour grouping slice with 15 hours retained for checks. Recommendations retain all 50 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce selected drafting and coordination work while retaining teaching and course judgement.
reach: Discuss course revision proposals with an instructional coordinator
skills_to_grow: Use shared calendars with clear permissions
role.ambitious_version: Maintain a checked course-planning collection that supports varied learners and makes course review easier.
